reason: The copy is each_b's body (CPY list_n .. BNE next_b) verbatim, entered with the same Y = list_b+1 and the same X; each_b's only other entry is LDY #0 from each_a, unchanged. Paths: CPY=list_n -> BEQ next_a (same target, same regs/flags); need,Y=0 or slot 0 -> next_b (the loop again, as the original's BRA each_b would reach); BCC below and the a-is-player fall-through, now BRA below (BRA leaves flags; .below reloads Y from list_b and reads only X, list_slot, need, so A/flags differences are moot - and there are none). Memory writes identical (STY list_b only). No other references to each_b/next_b/below (grep). Stack untouched. irq1_handler sees the same writes in the same order. Branch ranges: copy at &9855-&9874, BEQ next_a forward a few bytes, BEQ/BNE next_b back <30 bytes, BRA below back to &9842 about 50 bytes: all in range and in page &98, so no taken-branch page penalty (original BRA each_b &9858->&9826 also same page, 3 cycles). Indexed reads (list_slot,Y abs &B780; need,Y abs &001F; list_slot,X) are the same instructions with the same indices, so the same page-crossing cycles. Saving: 3 cycles each next_b reached (BRA each_b gone); the a-is-player path that reaches .below through the copy pays BRA below (+3) instead of falling through, netting 0 there, never worse. Bytes: +30 copied (CPY zp 2, BEQ 2, STY zp 2, LDA abs,Y 3, TAY 1, LDA need,Y abs 3, BEQ 2, TYA 1, BEQ 2, CMP abs,X 3, BCC 2, LDY abs,X 3, BNE 2, BRA 2) minus BRA each_b 2 = 28 bytes larger (claim -28 as a saving). Downstream layout shift is a speed matter for the gate, not semantics.
